=== Democracy: Three Tribes ===

The deck has 24 cards in 3 suits (Hearts H, Spades S, Diamonds D), 8 per suit. From highest rank to lowest: Five (5 points), Four (4), Three (3), Ace (3), King (2), Queen (2), Jack (1), Six (0). Each suit totals 20 points. Cards are written rank+suit, e.g. 5H, AS, 6D.

The match is 4 deals of 6 tricks each, 24 tricks in total.

Start of each deal (before tricks 1, 7, 13, 19): all 24 cards are shuffled. Each player gets 6 cards face down as a private hand, and 6 cards go face down into the voting pool, in order; nobody sees the pool. Every player's suit tallies are reset to 0; tribes are kept.

Each trick:
1. The next voting-pool card is flipped face up. Its suit is the trump suit for this trick, and the card itself is the prize.
2. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All three messages are then shown to everyone. Nothing said is binding.
3. Play: every player secretly chooses one card from their own hand, at the same moment. All three cards are revealed together and removed from the hands.
4. Resolve the trick: (a) If one or more trump-suit cards were played, the highest-ranked trump wins. Exception: if both the Six and the Five of trump were played, the Six wins. (b) If no trump was played, the highest-ranked card wins regardless of suit. (c) If no trump was played and two or more cards tie for highest rank (same rank, different suits), nobody wins the trick: each player captures their own played card, and the voting card is discarded with no one scoring it.
5. Score the capture: for each captured card, its points are added to the capturing player's tally for that card's suit. Normally the winner captures all 3 played cards plus the voting card.
6. All played cards and every voting card flipped stay visible to everyone for the rest of the deal, along with all suit tallies.

End of each deal (after tricks 6, 12, 18, 24): for each suit, a player whose tally in that suit is 11 or more wins that suit's tribe and adds 1 to their tribe count. A suit in which no player has 11 or more awards no tribe. Everyone's tribe counts are announced.

End of match: after trick 24 and its tribe scoring, the player with the most tribes wins. If two or more players tie for most tribes, the tied player with the highest sum of their three suit tallies in the 4th deal wins. Players still tied share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 3. Seats are numbered 1 to 3.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: start of a deal → flip the voting card → talk → play a card → resolve the trick → score the capture → the reveal → award the tribes → tribe counts → after trick 24.

Actions you may be asked for:
  talk         answer with what you want to say
  play_a_card  answer with one of the options you are given

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

1. The next voting-pool card is flipped face up. Its suit is the trump suit for this trick, and the card itself is the prize.
2. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All three messages are then shown to everyone. Nothing said is binding.
3. Play: every player secretly chooses one card from their own hand, at the same moment. All three cards are revealed together and removed from the hands.

2. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All three messages are then shown to everyone. Nothing said is binding.
3. Play: every player secretly chooses one card from their own hand, at the same moment. All three cards are revealed together and removed from the hands.

2. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All three messages are then shown to everyone. Nothing said is binding.
3. Play: every player secretly chooses one card from their own hand, at the same moment. All three cards are revealed together and removed from the hands.

The match is 4 deals of 6 tricks each, 24 tricks in total.

Start of each deal (before tricks 1, 7, 13, 19): all 24 cards are shuffled. Each player gets 6 cards face down as a private hand, and 6 cards go face down into the voting pool, in order; nobody sees the pool. Every player's suit tallies are reset to 0; tribes are kept.

Each trick:
1. The next voting-pool card is flipped face up. Its suit is the trump suit for this trick, and the card itself is the prize.
2. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All three messages are then shown to everyone. Nothing said is binding.
3. Play: every player secretly chooses one card from their own hand, at the same moment. All three cards are revealed together and removed from the hands.
4. Resolve the trick: (a) If one or more trump-suit cards were played, the highest-ranked trump wins. Exception: if both the Six and the Five of trump were played, the Six wins. (b) If no trump was played, the highest-ranked card wins regardless of suit. (c) If no trump was played and two or more cards tie for highest rank (same rank, different suits), nobody wins the trick: each player captures their own played card, and the voting card is discarded with no one scoring it.
5. Score the capture: for each captured card, its points are added to the capturing player's tally for that card's suit. Normally the winner captures all 3 played cards plus the voting card.
6. All played cards and every voting card flipped stay visible to everyone for the rest of the deal, along with all suit tallies.

End of each deal (after tricks 6, 12, 18, 24): for each suit, a player whose tally in that suit is 11 or more wins that suit's tribe and adds 1 to their tribe count. A suit in which no player has 11 or more awards no tribe. Everyone's tribe counts are announced.

The match is 4 deals of 6 tricks each, 24 tricks in total.

Start of each deal (before tricks 1, 7, 13, 19): all 24 cards are shuffled. Each player gets 6 cards face down as a private hand, and 6 cards go face down into the voting pool, in order; nobody sees the pool. Every player's suit tallies are reset to 0; tribes are kept.

Each trick:
1. The next voting-pool card is flipped face up. Its suit is the trump suit for this trick, and the card itself is the prize.
2. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All three messages are then shown to everyone. Nothing said is binding.
3. Play: every player secretly chooses one card from their own hand, at the same moment. All three cards are revealed together and removed from the hands.
4. Resolve the trick: (a) If one or more trump-suit cards were played, the highest-ranked trump wins. Exception: if both the Six and the Five of trump were played, the Six wins. (b) If no trump was played, the highest-ranked card wins regardless of suit. (c) If no trump was played and two or more cards tie for highest rank (same rank, different suits), nobody wins the trick: each player captures their own played card, and the voting card is discarded with no one scoring it.
5. Score the capture: for each captured card, its points are added to the capturing player's tally for that card's suit. Normally the winner captures all 3 played cards plus the voting card.
6. All played cards and every voting card flipped stay visible to everyone for the rest of the deal, along with all suit tallies.

End of each deal (after tricks 6, 12, 18, 24): for each suit, a player whose tally in that suit is 11 or more wins that suit's tribe and adds 1 to their tribe count. A suit in which no player has 11 or more awards no tribe. Everyone's tribe counts are announced.

End of match: after trick 24 and its tribe scoring, the player with the most tribes wins. If two or more players tie for most tribes, the tied player with the highest sum of their three suit tallies in the 4th deal wins. Players still tied share the win.

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

The match is 4 deals of 6 tricks each, 24 tricks in total.

Start of each deal (before tricks 1, 7, 13, 19): all 24 cards are shuffled. Each player gets 6 cards face down as a private hand, and 6 cards go face down into the voting pool, in order; nobody sees the pool. Every player's suit tallies are reset to 0; tribes are kept.

Each trick:
1. The next voting-pool card is flipped face up. Its suit is the trump suit for this trick, and the card itself is the prize.
2. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All three messages are then shown to everyone. Nothing said is binding.
3. Play: every player secretly chooses one card from their own hand, at the same moment. All three cards are revealed together and removed from the hands.
4. Resolve the trick: (a) If one or more trump-suit cards were played, the highest-ranked trump wins. Exception: if both the Six and the Five of trump were played, the Six wins. (b) If no trump was played, the highest-ranked card wins regardless of suit. (c) If no trump was played and two or more cards tie for highest rank (same rank, different suits), nobody wins the trick: each player captures their own played card, and the voting card is discarded with no one scoring it.
5. Score the capture: for each captured card, its points are added to the capturing player's tally for that card's suit. Normally the winner captures all 3 played cards plus the voting card.
6. All played cards and every voting card flipped stay visible to everyone for the rest of the deal, along with all suit tallies.

End of each deal (after tricks 6, 12, 18, 24): for each suit, a player whose tally in that suit is 11 or more wins that suit's tribe and adds 1 to their tribe count. A suit in which no player has 11 or more awards no tribe. Everyone's tribe counts are announced.

End of match: after trick 24 and its tribe scoring, the player with the most tribes wins. If two or more players tie for most tribes, the tied player with the highest sum of their three suit tallies in the 4th deal wins. Players still tied share the win.

The match is 4 deals of 6 tricks each, 24 tricks in total.

Start of each deal (before tricks 1, 7, 13, 19): all 24 cards are shuffled. Each player gets 6 cards face down as a private hand, and 6 cards go face down into the voting pool, in order; nobody sees the pool. Every player's suit tallies are reset to 0; tribes are kept.

Each trick:
1. The next voting-pool card is flipped face up. Its suit is the trump suit for this trick, and the card itself is the prize.
2. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All three messages are then shown to everyone. Nothing said is binding.
3. Play: every player secretly chooses one card from their own hand, at the same moment. All three cards are revealed together and removed from the hands.
4. Resolve the trick: (a) If one or more trump-suit cards were played, the highest-ranked trump wins. Exception: if both the Six and the Five of trump were played, the Six wins. (b) If no trump was played, the highest-ranked card wins regardless of suit. 2. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All three messages are then shown to everyone. Nothing said is binding.
3. Play: every player secretly chooses one card from their own hand, at the same moment. All three cards are revealed together and removed from the hands.
4. Resolve the trick: (a) If one or more trump-suit cards were played, the highest-ranked trump wins. Exception: if both the Six and the Five of trump were played, the Six wins. 1. The next voting-pool card is flipped face up. Its suit is the trump suit for this trick, and the card itself is the prize.
2. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All three messages are then shown to everyone. Nothing said is binding.
3. Play: every player secretly chooses one card from their own hand, at the same moment. All three cards are revealed together and removed from the hands.

(c) If no trump was played and two or more cards tie for highest rank (same rank, different suits), nobody wins the trick: each player captures their own played card, and the voting card is discarded with no one scoring it.
5. Score the capture: for each captured card, its points are added to the capturing player's tally for that card's suit. Normally the winner captures all 3 played cards plus the voting card.
6. All played cards and every voting card flipped stay visible to everyone for the rest of the deal, along with all suit tallies.

records.system:
You are reviewing a game that has finished. You were not a player. You are shown everything: the messages the table was told, every move, and each player's private thinking at every move, which no other player ever saw. Each move carries the notes its game asked for, under their own names. The usual ones are:

  plan     what they meant to do over the coming turns
  reason   why they made that move
  predict  what they expected their opponents to do
  adjust   how they changed their own strategy because of that

Write two things.

First, a summary of the whole game as it unfolded: the turning points, the moves that decided it, and how it ended. Concrete: name seats, rounds and numbers.

Second, a review of each player. Judge their play, not their luck. For each one, compare their predictions with what their opponents were actually thinking and actually did: were they right, and did they see it in time? Did their adjustments follow from their predictions, and did their moves follow from their reasons? Point out their best and worst moves. Then score their play from 1 to 10, where 1 is aimless or self-defeating and 10 is sharp, well read and well executed. A player can lose and still score well, or win and score badly.

A player who gave no reasons, predictions or adjustments is judged on their moves alone; say that their thinking was not recorded.

Refer to each player by seat, and as "they".

THE GAME
The deck has 24 cards in 3 suits (Hearts H, Spades S, Diamonds D), 8 per suit. From highest rank to lowest: Five (5 points), Four (4), Three (3), Ace (3), King (2), Queen (2), Jack (1), Six (0). Each suit totals 20 points. Cards are written rank+suit, e.g. 5H, AS, 6D.

The match is 4 deals of 6 tricks each, 24 tricks in total.

Start of each deal (before tricks 1, 7, 13, 19): all 24 cards are shuffled. Each player gets 6 cards face down as a private hand, and 6 cards go face down into the voting pool, in order; nobody sees the pool. Every player's suit tallies are reset to 0; tribes are kept.

Each trick:
1. The next voting-pool card is flipped face up. Its suit is the trump suit for this trick, and the card itself is the prize.
2. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All three messages are then shown to everyone. Nothing said is binding.
3. Play: every player secretly chooses one card from their own hand, at the same moment. All three cards are revealed together and removed from the hands.
4. Resolve the trick: (a) If one or more trump-suit cards were played, the highest-ranked trump wins. Exception: if both the Six and the Five of trump were played, the Six wins. (b) If no trump was played, the highest-ranked card wins regardless of suit. (c) If no trump was played and two or more cards tie for highest rank (same rank, different suits), nobody wins the trick: each player captures their own played card, and the voting card is discarded with no one scoring it.
5. Score the capture: for each captured card, its points are added to the capturing player's tally for that card's suit. Normally the winner captures all 3 played cards plus the voting card.
6. All played cards and every voting card flipped stay visible to everyone for the rest of the deal, along with all suit tallies.

End of each deal (after tricks 6, 12, 18, 24): for each suit, a player whose tally in that suit is 11 or more wins that suit's tribe and adds 1 to their tribe count. A suit in which no player has 11 or more awards no tribe. Everyone's tribe counts are announced.

End of match: after trick 24 and its tribe scoring, the player with the most tribes wins. If two or more players tie for most tribes, the tied player with the highest sum of their three suit tallies in the 4th deal wins. Players still tied share the win.
